title: FFT Stage Architecture
description: A two-band diagram showing the three Python-side pieces of an FFT above the single hand-written assembly hot loop, with a highlighted language boundary and live execution counts for any FFT size.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Assembly Language
Software Architecture
chapter_title: The Butterfly in Assembly: A Complete FFT and Production Libraries

educational.topic: Deciding which code to hand-optimize by execution frequency
learningObjectives: Differentiate the Python-side and assembly-side parts of an FFT
Justify each placement using how often the code runs
Explain why the language boundary is crossed per stage rather than per butterfly
prerequisites: A radix-2 FFT has log2(N) stages of N/2 butterflies
Assembly costs far more developer time than Python

controls.label: Architecture box
controls.purpose: Reveal what a piece does, how often it runs, and why it sits on that side

controls.label: Boundary arrow
controls.purpose: Reveal what crosses the language boundary

simulationModel.modelType: Static architecture diagram with frequency counts derived from FFT size
assumptions: Radix-2 decimation-in-time, so every stage does exactly N/2 butterflies
The butterfly kernel is eight instructions, matching the chapter's listing
The twiddle table is computed once at startup rather than per transform
limitations: Counts instructions, not cycles; memory stalls are not modeled
Radix-4 and split-radix variants change the counts and are not shown

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison of execution frequency, with the payoff of optimizing each piece made explicit
keyQuestions: If you made this piece twice as fast, how many cycles would one transform save?
What would happen if assembly were called once per butterfly instead of once per stage?
commonMisconceptions: That the trigonometry is the expensive part because it looks expensive
That more assembly always means more speed
assessmentOpportunities: Argue against rewriting the bit-reversal permutation in assembly
